chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Ammar Al-Duhni, who said:
I heard Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah loves every grieving heart, and He loves every grateful servant.'

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will say to one of His servants on the Day of Judgment: 'Did you thank so-and-so?' He will say, 'No, I thanked You, O Lord.' He will say, 'You did not thank Me because you did not thank him.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The most thankful to Allah are those who are most thankful to the people.'
ai.seo_question: What is the connection between thanking God and thanking people in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia concept of 'shukr al-ni‘am' by linking divine love to both the humility of a grieving heart and the practical gratitude shown to fellow humans. It highlights that true thankfulness to God is incomplete without acknowledging the intermediaries of His blessings, a principle rooted in the Prophet’s saying, 'The most grateful to people is the most grateful to God.' This underscores the social dimension of worship, where recognizing human agency is an act of recognizing Divine providence.
